t: You're outside the Garrick Club, a private members' club founded in 1831 for actors and men of refinement to meet on equal terms. It takes its name from David Garrick, the eighteenth-century actor, playwright and theatre manager, who influenced nearly every part of theatrical practice in his day. Its members include actors, writers, journalists, judges and members of parliament. For most of its history it admitted only men, but in May 2024 members voted to acknowledge that the rules had never actually excluded women, so women can now be elected.
